examples.en: A ship checks its surroundings with radar.
A strange object showed up on the radar.

examples.ko: 공항 옆에 큰 레이더 한 대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A large radar stands next to the airport.
Radar can also find rain clouds.

examples.ko: 레이더가 고장 나서 비행기가 늦게 떴어요.
examples.en: The radar broke, so the plane took off late.
Work to install a new radar has begun.

explain: '레이더에 잡히다'처럼 무언가가 발견될 때 말해요. 날씨 뉴스에서는 '기상 레이더'가 나와요.
explain_en: It is used in '레이더에 잡히다' when something is detected. Weather news mentions '기상 레이더' (weather radar).

examples.en: The stitches in this embroidery are really delicate.
The stitches weren't even, so I sewed it again.
If you make the stitches small, the clothes are sturdier.
With hand sewing, care goes into every single stitch.

examples.ko: 바늘땀 사이가 너무 넓으면 금방 뜯어져요.
examples.en: If the gaps between stitches are too wide, it comes apart quickly.

examples.ko: 바늘땀이 보이지 않게 안쪽에서 꿰매 주세요.
examples.en: Please sew it from the inside so the stitches don't show.

explain: 바늘로 한 번 떠서 남은 자국 하나를 말해요. 줄여서 '땀'이라고도 하고, 손으로 정성껏 할 때 '한 땀 한 땀'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the single mark left each time the needle goes through the cloth. People shorten it to '땀', and say '한 땀 한 땀' for careful hand work.

examples.en: This pot is made of stainless steel, so it's sturdy.

examples.ko: 스테인리스 컵은 오래 써도 냄새가 안 나요.
examples.en: A stainless steel cup doesn't smell even after long use.
A stainless steel kitchen sink is easy to clean.

examples.ko: 스테인리스 숟가락은 한국 식당에서 흔히 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Stainless steel spoons are commonly seen in Korean restaurants.

examples.ko: 저는 플라스틱 대신 스테인리스 빨대를 써요.
examples.en: I use stainless steel straws instead of plastic.
Stainless steel doesn't rust easily.

explain: '스테인리스'는 녹이 잘 슬지 않는 금속이에요. 한국 식당의 젓가락, 숟가락, 물컵이 대부분 스테인리스라서 일상에서 아주 자주 보이는 소재예요. 줄여서 '스뎅'이라고도 하는데 이건 일상 대화에서만 써요.
explain_en: 스테인리스 is a metal that does not rust easily. Chopsticks, spoons, and cups in Korean restaurants are mostly stainless steel, so it is a very common everyday material. People also say 스뎅 in casual talk, but only in conversation.

examples.en: The delivery box was full of styrofoam.
Styrofoam is thrown away separately.
The fish box is made of styrofoam, so it's light.
I got hot coffee in a styrofoam cup.
My child made a boat out of styrofoam.
Bits of styrofoam were scattered on the floor.

explain: 원래 상품 이름에서 왔지만 지금은 흰색 발포 플라스틱을 두루 부르는 말이에요. 포장 상자나 일회용 컵 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It started as a product name but now generally refers to white foam plastic. It often comes up when talking about packing boxes or disposable cups.

examples.ko: 산속에 작은 오두막이 한 채 있어요.
examples.en: There is one small hut in the mountains.
It rained, so we went inside the hut.
Grandfather lives alone in a hut in the forest.
We built a fire in front of the hut.
Though the hut was shabby, it was warm in winter.

examples.ko: 나무로 직접 오두막을 지어 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to build a hut myself out of wood.

explain: 작고 허름하게 지은 집을 말해서 '펜션'이나 '별장'처럼 깔끔한 느낌은 없어요. 산이나 숲, 바닷가에 있는 단순한 집에 써요. 동화나 이야기에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means a small, rough house, so it lacks the tidy feel of 펜션 or 별장. It fits a simple home in the mountains, forest or by the sea. It often appears in fairy tales and stories.

examples.en: There is a spring inside the ballpoint pen.
The bed spring is broken and makes a noise.
I sprang up like a spring and caught the ball.
The child rolled a spring toy down the stairs.
If you press the spring hard, it pops back out.
The springs inside the mattress are old and have stretched.

explain: '스프링'이라고도 말해요. 볼펜, 침대, 장난감처럼 눌렀다 놓으면 되돌아오는 부품에 써요. '용수철 장난감'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: People also say '스프링'. It is used for parts that return to shape after being pressed, like in pens, beds and toys. It can also go before another noun, as in '용수철 장난감'.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 주방이 협소해서 요리하기 불편해요.
examples.en: Our kitchen is cramped, so it's inconvenient to cook.

examples.ko: 협소한 공간에서도 쓸 수 있는 접이식 책상을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a folding desk that can be used even in a tight space.

examples.ko: 가게가 너무 협소하면 손님이 오래 머물기 어려워요.
examples.en: If a shop is too cramped, it's hard for customers to stay long.
The parking lot is small, so please use public transportation.

examples.ko: 직원이 늘어서 사무실이 협소해졌다고 다들 말해요.
examples.en: Everyone says the office has become cramped because we hired more people.

examples.ko: 이 방은 협소하지만 햇빛이 잘 들어서 좋아요.
examples.en: This room is small, but I like it because it gets a lot of sunlight.

explain: '좁다'와 비슷하지만 '협소하다'는 공간이나 면적이 좁아서 불편하다는 말을 정중하게 할 때 써요. 안내문이나 부동산, 뉴스에서 잘 어울려요. 옷이 좁거나 마음이 좁을 때는 '좁다'를 쓰고, 반대말은 '넓다'예요.
explain_en: It is similar to '좁다', but '협소하다' is used to say politely or formally that a space or area is too small to be comfortable. It fits notices, real estate and the news. For tight clothes or a narrow mind, use '좁다'; the opposite is '넓다'.
